correctness.rationale: For every even g>=8, the proposed residue set R_g modulo 4g+3 is sum-avoiding and its complement is covered by four translates using selected prefix elements. These two identities prove the greedy induction, while the explicit circular-gap structure proves minimality of the eventual characteristic period; the odd and small-even cases are elementary specializations. Direct finite generation and independent residue checks agree with the formulas over the stated verification ranges.

originality.rationale: Van Berkel--Bosma arXiv:2609.18522v1 explicitly presents the all-parameter period and preperiod formulas as conjectures. Its proved range g<=2f-1 supplies no case with f=1 and g>1, apart from separately handled boundary/small cases, while its general f=1 column is supported computationally only over finite ranges. Exact and synonymous searches found no proof of the complete f=1 family or the modulus 4g+3 residue description. The main residual risk is unindexed contemporaneous work because the motivating preprints are extremely recent.

value.rationale: The result proves an infinite one-parameter column of both principal periodicity conjectures, gives a closed-form description of every term of S_{1,g}, determines minimal preperiod and period lengths, and yields exact natural densities. The proof isolates a reusable modular mechanism: a sum-avoiding residue set whose complement is covered by translates from a finite selected prefix.
